quest.title: Lost in the Sands
quest.description: In Aaru Village, there is a merchant from Mondstadt who needs help from adventurers.
quest.rewards_formatted: Adventure EXP x350, Primogem x40, Mora x40000, Hero's Wit x3, Mystic Enhancement Ore x3

dialogues.text: Oh! Hello there! Judging from your attire, I take it you're not from around here? We don't get a lot of other outsiders here, I clocked you as being from somewhere else the moment I laid eyes on you.
*sigh* Making a living here is tough for outsiders.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: From what you're saying... You're also from somewhere else, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Bonifaz
dialogues.text: You can tell? My name's Bonifaz. My associate and I traveled to Sumeru City from Mondstadt to trade in some supplies. We're in the desert on the request of a researcher from the Akademiya.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You came to the desert from Mondstadt to do business...?

dialogues.speaker: Bonifaz
dialogues.text: Of course. Since you managed to make your way to a place as remote as this, you two must have been around the block too, I suppose?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Of course! And we know your hometown pretty well too!

dialogues.speaker: Bonifaz
dialogues.text: Well now! Then speaking of which, you must also know what sets us Mondstadters apart from others.

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: That's right! What we Mondstadters value most of all is freedom.

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: How does that saying go again?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: "Go with the wind"!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ...Come on, it's actually "let the wind lead"!

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: Yes, right, right! That's the one!

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: When the north wind began to blow, some dandelion seeds were blown across the sea to Inazuma, while others were swept away to Liyue.

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: As for me, I guess I was favored by the Anemo Archon. I didn't stop at Liyue and got blown all the way to Sumeru.

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: The climate and way of life here might be a far cry from that of Mondstadt, but I'm here, and I intend to make the best of things.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon gets it... But you just said that it's hard for outsiders to make a living here, right? Did something happen?

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: Oh, well, I accepted that Akademiya researcher's commission, didn't I...?

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: Tirzad — that's the researcher's name. He took two mercenaries with him to look for some ruins, probably for some archaeological research. I don't really know much about Akademiya stuff.

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: In addition to providing them with some supplies, my associate and I also rented a few Sumpter Beasts out to them.

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: Nachtigal, my associate, was worried that they'd struggle to steer the Sumpter Beasts, so he decided to go with them.

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: We originally arranged to use a Dusk Bird to send messages every once in a while, so that I could be informed of their progress or raise supplies to send to them as the situation required.

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: We did exchange messages this way at first, but I haven't heard a peep from them for the last two days...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon hopes there wasn't any sort of accident...

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: That's what I've been worrying about! That's why I was thinking about posting a commission with the Adventurers' Guild, but as they say, what good's a distant well when you're already parched...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Oh? Well, isn't this a coincidence!

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: So, you're young adventurers! But the desert is still a dangerous place. Wouldn't it be better for locals or adventurers with more experience to do this...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Are you underestimating us? Hmph! You've left Mondstadt, so maybe you're out of the loop...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #But you should know that {NICKNAME} isn't just any ordinary adventurer. {F#She's}{M#He's} an Honorary Knight of the Knights of Favonius!

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: #Huh? Wait. Then you must be... the celebrated {NICKNAME}...?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Oh! Then you have heard? That's right, this is the renowned {NICKNAME}! And Paimon is the famed Paimon!

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: Goodness gracious! Please excuse my rudeness! I never expected to meet a big hero in a place like this! And... And a little hero, too!

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: In that case, I have nothing more to say. I just worry that you may have some other important missions at hand, like saving a city or something, and don't have the time for a menial commission like this one...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh... It's not like we're always doing over-the-top stuff like that... We take ordinary commissions, too!

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: You mean you'll take this commission? That's fantastic! I knew heroes had hearts of gold. Of course you wouldn't turn your backs on someone at death's very door!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We haven't agreed to anything yet... And anyway, don't just throw "death" around like that, you'll jinx people!

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: Ah... Then I'll just have to return to the city alone and submit a commission to the Adventurers' Guild... But by the time someone accepts the commission, those four could already be... Alas...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Hmm...

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: If you two could take a little time out of your busy schedules to take this commission, I'll definitely come up with some way to make it worth your while! Right, that researcher from the Akademiya is also quite the generous client...

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: #I can picture it now: Just as they run into some trouble, {NICKNAME}, a true hero, descends from the heavens to save them!

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: That should secure you double the payment, right? This deal is a sure bet!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Hm... What do you think we should do, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: If they're in danger, we have to help them.

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: Great, fantastic! There's hope for my Cyrus yet!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: ..."Cyrus"?

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: Yes, Cyrus is the name of one of the Sumpter Beasts I rented to them.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? "Cyrus"? But isn't that...

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Does the actual Cyrus know about this?

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: ...Huh? W—Well...

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: ...Haha, it's fine, just don't tell him! No one will know!

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: Ahem, anyway, the researcher and the others left the village and headed west. The trails here are a bit hard to make out, but you should be able to find them by following the footprints.

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: I'll leave the rest to you two!

choices.text: We'll do it for the Mora.

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: That's right! Though that doesn't mean every Mondstadter is a lush. I hear that the one over at Dawn Winery isn't actually so fond of drinking... How can I put this? Everyone is free to drink or not drink.

response.speaker: Bonifaz
response.text: Right — what I meant to say was that what we Mondstadters value most is freedom.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: #{NICKNAME}, Paimon, it's good to see you! I've got an urgent commission I'd like to give you two.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: The commissioner is a Mondstadt merchant who is currently in Aaru Village. According to him, his associate and the Sumpter Beasts they leased out to an Akademiya researcher have been missing in the desert for a while now...

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: He's hoping that a highly experienced adventurer can take this commission and confirm the status of his associate and the Sumpter Beasts.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: You're both highly experienced adventurers, so a commission like this should be a cinch for you, I hope?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Missing in the desert... That certainly is worrying. Let's go take a look, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Katheryne
dialogues.text: The commissioner is named Bonifaz, and he's still in Aaru Village now. He can fill you in on the specifics. Safe travels, you two.

talks.objective: Go to Aaru Village and look for the merchant from Mondstadt

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (He's dressed like an Akademiya researcher, but why does he reek of booze...?)
Th—Think you can mess with me and scam me?! *hic*
J—Jebrael, you useless dolt! How long have we been going? You know... only to get stuck...
Ugh... If it wasn't for this busted stone slate...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Whoa, Paimon thinks he's drunk! There's no way we can talk with him now. Let's go ask someone else.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello, we're...
Did you guys... also fall down here?
The desert's no place for outsiders. If you have a way back, I suggest you take it as soon as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Looks like talking to us is the last thing he wants to do... Let's try someone else.)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Could this be Nachtigal, the associate that Bonifaz was telling us about?)
Uh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: (Oh? He doesn't seem well. Paimon thinks he's resting... Let's not disturb him...)

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Father, I'm back! Oh? Is Nachtigal doing better?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: #Right, Paimon and {NICKNAME} told me all about what happened! How can you just ignore people, father? Really, when is that temperament of yours ever going to change?

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Jeht explains the situation to the three of them.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That means we've completed Bonifaz's commission, right? After all, he only asked us to confirm the safety of the archaeology team as well as that of the Sumpter Beasts...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Bonifaz!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What happened!?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Bonifaz and Nachtigal are colluding to blackmail me... *sob*... That despicable Mondstadter came all the way to Sumeru just to extort me, I swear...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Is he still drunk...?

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: Mr. Tirzad, was the price not already agreed upon after our discussion? You even confirmed it yourself, so why are you telling a different story now?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I usually have my hands full with research matters, and I've never dealt with business people such as you before. How was I supposed to know the rules around pricing...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: If Jeht hadn't told me that you highballed me, I'd still be foolish enough to think that I scored a great deal!

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: Well...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: *sigh* I'm really sorry, Nachtigal. Father had told me after the fact that I shouldn't have shared it with Tirzad.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Eh...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oof... Why's Paimon getting the feeling that Jeht managed to offend all three people by saying that?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: That's it! I'm... I'm laying you all off! There's a limit to how much bullying I'll take! *sob*

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: That's not fair, Tirzad! Nachtigal and Bonifaz are in the wrong here, but father and I didn't do anything wrong!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Besides, didn't we only get stuck in this place because you insisted on coming here? Then you started throwing tantrums after that fall and drank even though you clearly can't hold your liquor...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: You might have the body of an adult, but you've been acting like a little baby. Haha.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: You... You!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jeht, that's enough. Tirzad looks like he might faint from rage! Now isn't the time to fight. What we should be doing is putting our heads together so we can get ourselves out of this mess.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Ooh! Someone's talking sense... So, that crook Bonifaz commissioned you to come look for me? And you're famous adventurers, you say?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Well, I'd like to hire you to get me out of this archon-forsaken place. At this rate, forget my research, even my very life will be cut short!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Since you're famous adventurers, surely you're more reliable than they are?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #(Is this the double payment Bonifaz mentioned...? What should we do, {NICKNAME}?)

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Now's not the time for bickering. Let's focus on getting out of here first.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're right, finding a way out together is what's most important right now. Any other complaints can be addressed once we're somewhere safe.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: That's right. See, Tirzad? If you could think as sensibly as Paimon, we wouldn't have gotten ourselves stuck in this situation.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jeht...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I just explored a little bit up ahead and found what looks to be ruins. Maybe there's an exit leading to the surface in there?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Desert ruins don't constitute a safe place! And I'm not going anywhere with such unreliable people...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But you're a researcher, aren't you? Shouldn't you be thrilled to have ruins to investigate?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I—I'm an Indoorsology researcher! I should be working indoors and poring over documents... Unlike some adventurers who go stark raving bananas when they see a pile of old ruins...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Oh, you...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Don't waste your breath on him, Jeht. Just let him stay here if he wants to.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: But father...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: He's our employer, so he has the right to decide what he does and doesn't want to do. We just have to do our jobs.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ah, there he goes...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: We'll come back after father and I find a safe path. If he doesn't want to come with us, then he can just wait here!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: And now there goes Jeht... What should we do?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: We can't just wait here.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You're right, let's go find a way out of here.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Are... Are you going to ditch me? The payment for the commission is negotiable, so don't leave me here with this crook from Mondstadt...

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: I've kept quiet up until now, but Bonifaz and I are not crooks. What shady businessmen would offer such comprehensive after-sales care?

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: Think about it, Mr. Tirzad, we could have simply received our payment and left it at that. But instead, we let ourselves end up in the same boat as you!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: ...I guess that makes sense? But I'm not staying here either way — I'd feel more comfortable in the company of experienced adventurers.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But you're still rip-roaring drunk... Why don't you stay here and sleep it off first?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I am not drunk! I'm fine! I'm coming with you guys! Don't leave me behind... *sob*

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Th—Then we should get going. We should be able to catch up with Jeht and the others.

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: I'll wait here for now — I doubt the road ahead will be suitable for the Sumpter Beasts. Good luck.

talks.objective: Talk to the fourth person in the distance

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Hello?
Oh? Are you the newly fallen?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? What do you mean "newly fallen"?
Oh? Do you have a way out?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? We accepted Bonifaz's commission to come look for Tirzad's archaeological team...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Bonifaz? That merchant from Mondstadt? I know him. So, you want to find the archaeological team, huh? Let me think... Oh, isn't that us? I'm Jeht. Tirzad... sort of hired me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: He said that he hadn't gotten any word from you guys in a while, and he was worried that something might have happened to you, so he asked us to come and check things out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon wonders if he was the one who was taking a break...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Are all Mondstadters so paranoid? What do you mean "a while"? It's only been a day...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: If it weren't for that bad fall and the heatstroke that Nachtigal had, we'd also be trying to find a way out.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: So, this pit is...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: That's right, the desert is an incredible place. One minute, you're looking at solid ground, the next, you step directly into a trap. And as you can see, we're trapped here now.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Did you guys just get here? Or do you have another way out? Still, we've searched all over this place, and there doesn't seem to be any way back to the surface.

response.speaker: Player
response.text: We have a wind glider.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: A wind glider! I heard Nachtigal talk about them before. They sound pretty great! To be honest, I'd love to give flying a try too! Wait a minute, now that I think about it, your lil' friend here doesn't seem to even need a wind glider to fly!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Can you teach me, lil' friend? How can I be as footloose and free as you? Er... I mean, as floaty?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon is nobody's "lil' friend"! Even Bonifaz knows that Paimon is famous!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #And {NICKNAME} here is just as famous as Paimon!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: All right, my renowned lil' friend Paimon, can you teach me? What do I have to do to float freely through the air like you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Uh, Paimon doesn't really have an answer for you there... {NICKNAME}...?

choices.text: If you practice hard enough, maybe a miracle will happen.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You can't just wake up one morning to find yourself floating!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #I see, so you must've hired Paimon to teach you how to fly, didn't you, {NICKNAME}? But since you're still using a wind glider, I suppose you haven't trained enough, huh...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Once you train enough, I'm sure you'll finally be able to fly freely without needing a wind glider!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #You seem like a really good teacher, Paimon! Can I hire you to teach me, too? Hey, {NICKNAME}, how much Mora will I need to hire Paimon?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Wow... You've got a wild imagination, huh? We don't have that sort of relationship.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Huh? But isn't it just like how Tirzad hired my father and me? And Nachtigal too! Surely I can also hire you as long as I have the Mora to spend?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #That's right! Paimon won't leave {NICKNAME}'s side.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Oh, that's a shame, then.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: By the way, have you seen Tirzad and my father?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: We have, but...

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You explain the situation with the others to Jeht.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Haha, I see. As I said before, Nachtigal must be having a tough time, what with the bad fall he took plus the heatstroke.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: As for my father, well, he's got a nasty temper — don't take it personally. And as for Tirzad, he's basically been throwing a tantrum since things stopped going smoothly.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That said, grouchy kids don't usually get that drunk...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: You're not wrong, Paimon! Haha. Sometimes father will have a few glasses as well, but I've never seen him get drunk before.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: How about this? We can go back together and I'll explain everything to my father. You guys don't wanna stay here too long, do you?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How could you say that? Of course Paimon would never leave your side!

choices.text: Everyone has their own special talents. There's no need to force it.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! Don't get bogged down with whether you can fly or not, Jeht. You should work towards something else! Like, a race with a Rishboland Tiger or something, hee-hee.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Who's Cyrus? Do we have someone on our team named Cyrus?

dialogues.speaker: Bonifaz
dialogues.text: Nachtigal doesn't worry me so much, but I do hope Cyrus comes back safe and sound...

talks.objective: Go to the area near the ruins together with Tirzad

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: We're here! Tirzad decided to come exploring with us.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: What now? You mean that researcher actually changed his mind?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Ugh...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: He knows the pros and cons, so naturally, he came along.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: All right, well, you'll get the chance to show off your skills soon enough! How should we enter the interior of the ruins? This is a researcher's specialty, right?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: This should be a piece of cake for you, right, Tirzad?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: O—Of course! I might be an Indoorsology researcher, but something as basic as this can't be too different from what's written in the books...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Watch this!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: ...Hmm, this is... There! That should do it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa, the door really opened!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Well, that's Mr. Tirzad for you!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Heh, that's what sets us professionals apart from the amateurs.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon wonders what it's like inside. Let's go in and take a look!

talks.objective: Explore up ahead through the long corridor

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Who are you? *hic* Thanks, but I'll pass. I can't manage another sip.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: If there's nothing else, leave as soon as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: It's a good thing nothing happened to Cyrus, or Bonifaz would be a weeping wreck.

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: *whimper*

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: We've been walking around for a while without making any progress, so why don't we take a little rest?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Are you kidding? It's hardly been any time at all and you're already thinking of resting?!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I said it before, didn't I? I'm an Indoorsology researcher! I should never have come out into the middle of nowhere like this...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wait a minute, Paimon's confused. Wasn't the archaeology mission your idea?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jeht, Jebrael, and Nachtigal only came because you hired them, right?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Yes, that's correct.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? So it was your idea, then why have you been dragging your feet this whole time?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: If we didn't know the truth, Paimon would think that Jebrael must've kidnapped you to get some legendary treasure in the ruins or something.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Haha, you're funny, Paimon! My father may be a grump, but he'd never do something like that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...D—Don't get mad at Paimon. Paimon's only telling it like it is!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: Don't bully Paimon.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I'm sorry. My father really isn't a bad guy, believe me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Then why is Tirzad so unmotivated?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: *sigh* It's because I don't care for the topic at all. If it wasn't for this accursed stone slate...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I'm always told to be original in my research and to find material that no one has ever worked on before.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: "What's the value or meaning of research if everyone is just following the herd or reproducing each other's work?" — or so I've been told.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: But what am I compared to such a long-standing academic tradition and all my seniors in research? I'm no academic genius, so what can I think of that others can't?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: There are no academic gaps left these days that I can identify and fill...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Paimon doesn't really get academic stuff either, but since this is your job, you should take it seriously.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I do! I give it my all! Why else would I have spent so much Mora to come to this archon-forsaken place...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Heh, it's funny, but this Scarlet Sand Slate was actually the research project of a relative of mine...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: She was originally a young researcher with limitless promise, but one day, she left the family behind and eloped with some wild boy from who knows where.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I heard that they fled into this desert back in those days. Unfortunately, I was a kid then and only saw her a few times. I can't even remember what she looked like.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: All the more reason to buck up! Since you're researching the same thing, there's a chance for a reunion, isn't there?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Fate is an unpredictable thing, after all.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Haha... Even if we really did meet again, and even if we really recognized each other, how could I even face her?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: The way I am now, I'm no different from a stray dog, living off the scraps thrown away by others...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Since I'm incapable of constructing any new theories, all I could do was take my chances in the field and see if I could dig up any new materials to base my paper on.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Though, when it comes to King Deshret, the academic community has long since concluded that he was just another self-destructive tyrant...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Speaking of which, she must have left this stone slate behind when she left back then because even she knew this lousy thing had no research value.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Haha, and yet I took it to be a treasure! Haha! This silly stone slate! I must have been out of my mind to think I'd really be able to stumble upon something.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Uh... Still, Paimon doesn't think you should lose heart!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Because... Because, um, we often make surprising discoveries while exploring ruins like these! Right, {NICKNAME}?

choices.text: There will at least be treasure chests, for sure.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Although those might not be much use to Tirzad...

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: None of you have ever done serious academic research. How could you possibly understand me or the difficulties of being a researcher...

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: Stop talking like a child. The Akademiya might control the path to academic publication, but they don't have a monopoly on knowledge itself.

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: If this is all you know about King Deshret, then you should have abandoned academia from the very beginning, because it's clear you won't get any results.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Father...

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: You? You're just a paid mercenary, what right do you have to comment on my ideas?

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: So far, you seem to have very little in the way of professional credentials as a researcher. That much you already admitted yourself.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Me? I'm—! You... You!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: Tirzad gets so worked up that the blood rushes to his head, causing him to faint...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Uh-oh, what happened? Will he be okay...?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: We should keep a closer eye on him after this and not let him drink any more. He must not have completely sobered up yet when father made him so mad that all the blood rushed to his head.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: That was weird, though. Why'd you have to get so mad at him?

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: ...We can't stop just because he keeps dragging his feet.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Huh? But we can't just leave him here either...

response.speaker: Jebrael
response.text: I'll stay behind to keep him safe. Meanwhile, you and Jeht keep looking for an exit.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Well... what should we do now, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Player
response.text: Time's a-wastin'.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: You're right... Let's keep exploring, then!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Leave Tirzad to my father, you'll have nothing to worry about. I'll come with you guys!

choices.text: It's also good to see everything with your own eyes.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: That's right! Paimon might not really get super difficult research, but... there's so much stuff in big ruins like these! If you take a good look around, there's got to be something you can write about, right?

talks.objective: Continue investigating the ruins with Jeht

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: (He looks like he's in a lot of pain, we probably shouldn't wake him up...)

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How familiar!
Beep?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa! It's moving!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hmm? Looks a lot like the one we just knocked down. Still... it doesn't look like it's going to attack us.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: On second thought, it can float in the air just like Paimon. Does that make them distant relatives?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon would sooner be related to a pigeon!
Beep... Beep?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #This thing's making weird noises again... Where's that sound coming from, anyway? And is it really not going to turn on us out of the blue? {NICKNAME}, don't let your guard down.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Can you try talking to it, Paimon? Look, you two are about the same size, so you should be able to talk to each other, right?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: How is Paimon supposed to talk to it?! Oh! You're messing with Paimon on purpose, aren't you?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Tee-hee.
Beep-boop. Beep.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: It looks like some sort of device.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Sh—Should we pick it up and try using it?
Beep...!!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eek! Gah, you scared Paimon!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: It doesn't seem to want to do that.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Eh? Can you understand it, Jeht?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Um... I can't understand the meaning, but I can get... the feeling?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wh—What a weird thing...
Beep-beep, beep.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Oh? I think it's a lot like you, Paimon. You both look really cute!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon told you, we're nothing alike!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Well, yeah, you're round and cute, Paimon, and it seems a little... pokey? But it's still very cute!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ugh... Paimon totally doesn't get your standards for "cute"...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: #Now isn't the time for this, {NICKNAME}.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #The way I see it, Paimon doesn't get it, but {NICKNAME} does.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: I don't know why it's here or what it's used for... But maybe Tirzad will understand if we can get him to take a look at it.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: You... Hmm? What should I call you anyhow?
Beep-boop?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Paimon floats, but you're a little lower off from the ground, so... I'll call you Benben!

response.speaker: Benben
response.text: Beep-beep!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: You like this name, too? That's great!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: How do those two even communicate...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: She is amazing, in a weird sort of way.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: #Benben, it must be boring hanging around here by yourself. Why don't you come with us? Needless to say, {NICKNAME} is pretty great, too.

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: As for Paimon... She might act a little superior, but she's a good kid who thinks about her companions. You'll definitely come to like her in time.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon doesn't act super-anything! Anyway, Paimon's not gonna fly lower for anyone! Otherwise, Paimon will breathe in a whole load of sand...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Come look for my father with us. He may look mean, but actually... Well, he actually is kind of mean. But that's just how he is with outsiders! He's nice once you get to know him!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: And even though Tirzad's a useless researcher, he's not actually a bad guy. Right, and you might even be able to save his research, Benben!

response.speaker: Benben
response.text: Beep-boop?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Well? Wanna come with us, Benben?

response.speaker: Benben
response.text: Beep... Bee-eep!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: That's great! It said yes!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Really? Are you guys really talking to each other?

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Don't worry, Paimon. Benben and I are already joined at the hip! Right, Benben?

response.speaker: Benben
response.text: Beep-beep!

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Hehe, well, let's go back to where my father is. Maybe Tirzad has already woken up.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Provided he doesn't open up his eyes only to see Jebrael and get so mad that he passes out again...

response.speaker: Jeht
response.text: Haha, you never know!

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: To be honest, Paimon kind of admires her in a way...

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Right? So that makes two of us!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Father, I brought another new friend back! Look, this is the friend we just met, its name is Benben.

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Oh, Tirzad's awake. Looks like things are going well with father.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I don't know how you came to that ridiculous conclusion, but... let's not discuss that for now. What I'm most concerned about now is, what is that thing?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Didn't I just introduce you? This is our new friend, Benben.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: This doesn't seem like something that could be classified as a "friend," could it?! Doesn't this look a little like the same thing that just attacked us?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: You don't have a lot of friends, do you, Tirzad?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: No, I don't... Wait, what does that have to do with this?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: You're way too uptight! You just need an open mind, and you'll be swimming in friends in no time. Isn't that right, Benben?

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: And you're too lax!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: So, you don't know what Benben is either, huh?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: It... must be related to the guards here. I don't know exactly how to operate it, though.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: But this unique model doesn't attack outsiders and can even communicate to a certain extent... I don't remember reading anything about this.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Tirzad!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Wh—What is it?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Isn't that amazing news?

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: This is the "material that no one has worked on before."

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Wait a minute, could it be? No, it's too early to celebrate just yet... Maybe I was too narrow-minded and just happened to not see any relevant prior research on it...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Maybe someone has already published ten treatises and thoroughly studied Benben's genealogy...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Why does this guy always jump to the worst conclusions...

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Wait a minute, something doesn't seem right about it.

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep... Beep...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: What is it, Benben? Are you—

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Ooh! Benben seems to be reacting to Tirzad's stone slate!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Tirzad, pick the stone slate up and walk towards Benben.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I hired you! Don't tell me what to do...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Whoa...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Ooh, Benben! You're amazing, Benben!

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Bee-eep. Beep!

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep-boop... Beep, Bee-eep!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Paimon doesn't completely understand what it's saying, but it seems happy!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: A small portion of the slate lit up. What does it mean? Do you have any idea, Tirzad?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Hmm... It's hard to say, only a portion was lit up. Besides, I've told you all before...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Rigor is key to academic research, and you don't want to jump to conclusions, right?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: O—Oh, yes, that's true.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Heh, looks like we'll just have to find a way to light up the rest of the stone slate. Right, Benben?

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep... Bee-eep.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: #Hold on, I have a serious request to make of you, {NICKNAME}.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Ahem, this has nothing to do with Jebrael or Jeht, so I kindly ask that you give us some space.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Huh? You gonna reveal some kind of secret? C'mon, I wanna hear it, too!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Jeht, mind your own business.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: But father, we're all companions here. Doesn't that make it our business?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Fine! I'll give you all the space you want. Let's go, Benben.

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: What's the matter? Why are you getting so serious all of a sudden...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Can you... help me take care of this stone slate?

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Huh? Isn't it really important?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: It is, and that's why I want you to take care of it! And to be honest, seeing it light up like that makes me uneasy...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I don't trust myself if something were to happen. Besides, that weird thing also seems to have some sort of response to it...

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That weird thing... You mean Benben? Wouldn't it be better to give the stone slate to Jeht to look after?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: No! Ahem... I mean, absolutely not.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: How do I put this? Alright. I don't trust Jebrael. I feel like he has an ulterior motive... and since Jeht is his daughter, they're obviously going to be in the same camp.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jebrael might be a man of few words, but Paimon thinks he's very reliable. Could you be overthinking this, Tirzad...?

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Jeht said it before, he's from the desert. Can you really trust the desert people? I'd sooner believe that Bonifaz didn't defraud me.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: #Hmm... What do you think, {NICKNAME}?

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: It can fit carrots and cabbages, so one more little stone slate shouldn't be a problem, right?

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: Thank you! You're the only ones I can rely on in this vast sea of sand!

response.speaker: Black Screen
response.text: You receive the Scarlet Sand Slate that Tirzad entrusted to you.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Fine, we'll take care of it for you for the time being.

response.speaker: Tirzad
response.text: You're a huge help!

choices.text: The stone slate isn't heavy either.

response.speaker: Paimon
response.text: Paimon guesses so...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Hey, are you done whispering to each other yet?

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Tirzad's ready to set off now. We should find an exit as soon as possible.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I don't need you to speak for me. Um... That said, I am indeed ready to set off whenever.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Great! It's been a productive day, and I've got a feeling that we'll find a way out in no time! Benben and I will go on ahead. Everyone else can follow us.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Jeht and Benben sure have hit it off. That's... good, right?

talks.objective: Continue exploring and open the door
Continue exploring and look for an exit
Follow the path and continue exploring

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: I can feel a breeze... The exit must be close by! Keep looking. We'll be out of here in no time.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Woohoo! We can finally leave!

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: ...Although it's certain to be nothing but sand for miles around out there.

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: At least we'll be able to see the sky.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: That's true!

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: Where... Where do you guys get all that energy from? First it's exploring, then it's fighting... Let's slow down a little...

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: You and father are the same age, aren't you, Tirzad? How many times have we stopped to rest so far?

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: The mind of a child, the body of an old man... Geez.

dialogues.speaker: Benben
dialogues.text: Beep beep... Bee-eep.

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I told you, I'm an Indoor... forget it. I'm the employer, so just listen to me!

dialogues.speaker: Black Screen
dialogues.text: Everyone rests with Tirzad for a while.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Oh? If it isn't Nachtigal!

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: There you are. When the door on the other side suddenly opened, I knew you'd found an exit. I brought Cyrus and the others over.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: Wow, that was pretty brave of you! What if it wasn't a shortcut at all, but a trap?

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: Heh, you've got a point.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: You mean that it didn't even occur to you?!

dialogues.speaker: Nachtigal
dialogues.text: Well, everything worked out fine in the end. We've reunited, haven't we? That's enough. By the way, we've got a new member here? That's great!

dialogues.speaker: Player
dialogues.text: That's a free Mondstadter for you.

dialogues.speaker: Paimon
dialogues.text: But it's better to be cautious at times like this!

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: But isn't it great that we don't have to double back to rendezvous? Now we can find the exit together!

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Follow the wind and find your way out. But don't let your guard down.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: Okay... got it!

talks.objective: Follow the direction of the wind to find the exit
Leave the pit through the exit

dialogues.speaker: Mirsad
dialogues.text: I thought it'd be a short and even bland trip into the desert. But we instead got ourselves into something so crazy. It was a little scary, but I can't say I dislike it.

dialogues.speaker: Omid
dialogues.text: I just wanted to make some easy Mora so that I could start a business, but the job almost cost me my life...

dialogues.speaker: Tirzad
dialogues.text: I've said what I've got to say... Ahem, it's time to look for Jeht and the others.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Let's get a move on, enough dawdling.

dialogues.speaker: Jebrael
dialogues.text: Don't stick your nose into other people's business... especially when your employer's concerned. I believe I've taught you better than that.

dialogues.speaker: Jeht
dialogues.text: B—But I think they're no longer "other people," are they?
